items.stem: What does the arrange-act-assert structure give a unit test?

options.text: A clear separation of setup, the single action under test, and the verification
options.rationale: Correct: AAA keeps tests readable by separating setup, action and assertion.

options.text: A guarantee the code has no bugs
options.rationale: Structure improves clarity but cannot guarantee bug-free code.
AAA is about structure, not execution topology.

options.text: A replacement for the production code
options.rationale: Tests verify code; they do not replace it.

items.explanation: Correct: AAA keeps tests readable by separating setup, action and assertion.

items.stem: Select TWO techniques for making asynchronous and timer-based JavaScript tests reliable.

options.text: Await the promise and assert both resolve and reject paths
options.rationale: Correct: awaiting and covering both outcomes makes async tests deterministic.

options.text: Use fake timers to advance time instead of real waiting
options.rationale: Correct: fake timers remove real delays and flakiness from timer tests.

options.text: Add fixed real sleeps and hope the operation finished
options.rationale: Real sleeps are slow and flaky.

options.text: Hit the live network so the test is realistic
options.rationale: Live network calls make unit tests slow and non-deterministic.

options.text: Ignore the reject path because it rarely happens
options.rationale: Untested error paths are a common source of real bugs.

items.explanation: Correct: awaiting and covering both outcomes makes async tests deterministic.

items.stem: Why is 100% line coverage not proof that code is correct?

options.text: Executing a line is not the same as asserting its behavior is right
options.rationale: Correct: coverage shows lines ran, not that outcomes were meaningfully asserted.

options.text: Coverage tools always report the wrong number
options.rationale: Coverage numbers are generally accurate; the issue is what they mean.
It is reachable; the point is it still does not prove correctness.
Coverage measures executed code, not performance.

items.explanation: Correct: coverage shows lines ran, not that outcomes were meaningfully asserted.
